resources.string: Leaf tags each worktree with the agent tool that made it, from the file the tool leaves in the worktree's git dir or from the folder it's in. Your rules come first. In a folder pattern, * stands for one folder name or part of one, ** for any number of folders, ~/ for your home folder and <repo> for the repository's folder. A pattern that starts with ** matches anywhere, and one that doesn't start with /, ~/, ** or <repo> is in the repository's folder.

What double-clicking a conflicted file and the banner's Resolve conflicts open. The other one stays in the file's menu. The external tool is the one that git mergetool runs (merge.guitool, then merge.tool), and the banner opens it on each conflicted file in turn, as git mergetool does; files it can't take, and repositories without one, open in the built-in resolver.

How the built-in resolver shows a file. Columns puts ours, the result and theirs side by side. Stacked puts ours and theirs on top and the result below at the full width, which suits a narrow or portrait screen. The resolver's toolbar switches it too.

Wrap lines that don't fit their column in the built-in resolver. Turned off, each line stays on one row, and every column scrolls sideways together, as in Meld. The resolver's toolbar has the same switch, Wrap lines.

Wrap long lines. Turned off, each line stays on one row, and the lines scroll sideways together: swipe sideways, use Shift and the wheel, or drag the scrollbar under the lines.
Turned off, each line of a diff stays on one row, and the lines scroll sideways together. The diff's header has the same switch.

resources.string: What Save writes into the file: the lines nobody changed, the changes that don't conflict, and a side for each conflict. Open conflicts are written as conflict markers.
In a merge, ours is the branch checked out, %1$s, and theirs is the branch being merged into it, %2$s.
In a rebase, ours is what the rebase builds on, %1$s, with the commits replayed so far, and theirs is the commit being replayed, %2$s.
In a cherry-pick, ours is the branch checked out, %1$s, and theirs is the commit being picked, %2$s.
In a revert, ours is the branch checked out, %1$s, and theirs is %2$s: the commit's changes, undone.
Ours is what was checked out, %1$s, and theirs is %2$s, such as a stash being applied.
